title: Vichy France
capsule: The État français (Vichy France) was the authoritarian French state established on 10 July 1940 when the National Assembly granted Marshal Philippe Pétain constituent power, formally abolishing the Third Republic. The regime collaborated with Nazi Germany, cooperating in the deportation of approximately 77,000 Jews from France to the extermination camps, and initially controlled metropolitan France south of the demarcation line plus the overseas empire; Germany occupied the southern zone in November 1942 (Case Anton) after the Allied landings in North Africa. The liberation of Paris on 25 August 1944 ended effective Vichy authority, and the state ceased to exist when de Gaulle's Provisional Government of the French Republic was formally recognized by the Allies in October 1944.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
